questions.question: What is meant by discontinuous variation?
options: Variation where features can take any numerical value within a range.
Variation where features fall into distinct, limited categories.
Variation that changes constantly throughout a person's life.
Variation caused only by environmental injuries.

questions.question: Which of the following describes continuous variation?
options: Features can take any value within a range, such as height.
Features are strictly limited to distinct categories, like blood group.
Features that are only passed down from one parent.
Features that never change regardless of the environment.

questions.question: Which of these human features is an example of discontinuous variation?
options: Body mass
Height
ABO blood group
Skin colour

questions.question: A student wants to collect primary data on a continuous variation feature in their class. Which measurement should they record?
options: Eye colour of each student
Ability to roll the tongue
Hand span in centimetres
Biological sex

questions.question: What type of graph is best used to display continuous data, such as the heights of students in a year group?
options: Bar chart
Pie chart
Histogram or line graph
Pictogram

questions.question: When plotting continuous variation data on a histogram, how should the data be organized on the horizontal (x) axis?
options: In distinct, non-overlapping category names (e.g., Blue, Brown, Green)
In continuous, touching intervals or ranges (e.g., 140-149 cm, 150-159 cm)
As individual names of each participant
In order of how much the environment affected them

questions.question: If a histogram showing the masses of a population of mice has a tall peak in the middle and slopes down on both sides, what does this tell us?
options: Most mice have extreme masses, either very light or very heavy.
There are only two distinct types of mice in the population.
Most mice have a mass near the average, with fewer mice being very light or very heavy.
The mass of the mice is determined entirely by a single gene.

questions.question: Which of the following is typically true about features that show continuous variation?
options: They are controlled by a single gene and unaffected by the environment.
They are usually influenced by many factors, including genetics, environment, and lifestyle.
They are only influenced by lifestyle and have no genetic basis.
They can only be passed down from the mother.

questions.question: Which type of chart is most appropriate for displaying discontinuous data, such as the number of students with different natural hair colours?
options: Line graph
Histogram
Scatter graph
Bar chart

questions.question: When plotting discontinuous variation data on a bar chart, how should the bars be drawn?
options: Touching each other to show a continuous range
With gaps between the bars to represent distinct categories
As a single continuous line connecting all data points
Only using different shades of a single colour

questions.question: A student looks at a bar chart of tongue-rolling ability in a school. One bar shows 'Rollers' and the other shows 'Non-rollers', with a clear gap between them. What does this graph indicate?
options: Tongue rolling is a continuous feature that changes daily.
The data is discontinuous, meaning people fit into one of two distinct categories.
Every student can roll their tongue if they practice.
The feature is heavily influenced by the school environment.

questions.question: What is the primary cause of discontinuous variation, such as whether a plant has red or white flowers?
options: It is usually caused only by genetics and is not affected by environment or lifestyle.
It is caused entirely by the amount of sunlight and water the plant receives.
It is caused by physical injuries during the plant's growth.
It is caused by a combination of soil pH and the age of the plant.

questions.question: When dogs reproduce, they always give birth to puppies rather than kittens or piglets. What concept does this illustrate?
options: Environmental variation
Species resemblance
Discontinuous variation
Continuous variation

questions.question: Why do brothers and sisters often look similar to each other and to their parents, but not completely identical?
options: They inherit features from both parents, creating a family resemblance.
They live in different houses and have completely different diets.
They only inherit features from their mother.
They copy each other's facial expressions over time.

questions.question: How are inherited features passed from parents to their offspring during reproduction?
options: Through the sharing of nutrients in the environment
When DNA is passed from parents to offspring
By learning and copying behaviors after birth
Through physical contact during early development

questions.question: Which of the following features is caused or changed primarily by an organism’s lifestyle and environment?
options: Blood group
Eye colour
Having a scar from an accident
Lobed or lobeless earlobes

questions.question: Which statement best describes the variation among offspring from the same parents?
options: Offspring are always genetically identical to one of their parents.
Offspring are identical to each other but different from their parents.
There is usually variation between offspring; they are not identical to their parents or each other.
Offspring show no variation because they have the same parents.

questions.question: If you compare a group of pet cats, which of the following statements about differences is true?
options: The differences between a cat and a dog are smaller than the differences between two cats.
The differences between two different species (like a cat and a rabbit) are greater than differences within a species (like two cats).
There are no physical differences between different species.
Differences within a species are always greater than differences between different species.

questions.question: What do scientists call the differences in features between individuals of the same species?
options: Adaptation
Evolution
Variation
Classification

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of variation caused only by the environment?
options: A scar from a bicycle accident
Having blue eyes
Being biological male or female
Having blood type AB
